_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 52-week trial; sarilumab 150 mg or 200 mg or placebo every two weeks added to background methotrexate, with escape/rescue for inadequate responders.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active RA who had an inadequate clinical response to methotrexate (MTX).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at Week 24.

nct_ctgov.title: Evaluation of Sarilumab (SAR153191/REGN88) on Top of Methotrexate in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; sarilumab 200 mg, 150 mg, or placebo every two weeks with concomitant conventional DMARD(s), with rescue after Week 12.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active RA who had an inadequate clinical response or were intolerant to one or more TNF-alpha antagonists.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at Week 24.

nct_ctgov.title: To Evaluate The Effect Of SAR153191 (REGN88) Added To Other RA Drugs In Patients With RA Who Are Not Responding To Or Intolerant Of Anti-TNF Therapy (SARIL-RA-TARGET)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 3%): neutropenia, increased ALT, injection site erythema, upper respiratory infections, and urinary tract infections. In the placebo-controlled population, neutropenia occurred in 7% (150 mg) and 10% (200 mg) vs 0.2% placebo. Most common serious adverse reactions were infections; serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death are the principal risk (boxed warning).
target_moa: Sarilumab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody (IL-6 receptor antagonist) that binds to soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors (sIL-6R and mIL-6R) and inhibits IL-6-mediated signaling.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS. Patients treated with KEVZARA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death; opportunistic infections have also been reported.

rems.type: REMS will not be required for this product; safe use information provided through labeling and a Medication Guide.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for Kevzara use in active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) in patients 63 kg or greater.

summary.text: KEVZARA (sarilumab) received a standard (non-expedited) BLA approval on May 22, 2017 for moderately to severely active RA in DMARD inadequate responders. Efficacy was established in two phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (Study 11072 and Study 10832) with the primary endpoint of ACR20 at Week 24. The original BLA (received October 30, 2015) received a Complete Response action on October 28, 2016 due to manufacturing site issues; Sanofi resubmitted March 22, 2017. No REMS was required, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class.

citations.quote: Efficacy of sarilumab at doses of 150 mg and 200 mg every two weeks was established in two phase 3 trials in patients with RA.
